$comment: The cyclomatic-complexity ratchet for components, checked by
scripts/check-complexity.mjs and wired after Test in ci.yml's ui job.
Read that script's header first: it explains why the scan is .tsx-only
and why the pins are the only thing standing between this and a gate
`max` is the ceiling oxlint applied when this block was measured, not a
setting: eslint/complexity's max has no CLI switch and 20 is the rule's
own default. It is pinned so a moved upstream default fails loudly
instead of silently redrawing every number below. The pinned oxlint
version in package.json is the other half of that guarantee.
Each entry pins a file's WORST function and how many are OVER the ceiling;
both only ever go down. `total` is recorded, never enforced. Up is a
regression; down without lowering the pin is a stale pin and also fails;
a file absent here must have zero. Collapsing branches is the fix —
four `else if` arms assigning the same two variables are one ternary
pair — and pulling a body out into a helper is the other.
The debt standing the day the gate landed: 17 files, 20 functions over
the ceiling, 2674 total decision paths across the components scanned.
